pipeline_name: Mumbai Regional Natural Gas Pipeline Network

validity.recommendation: no change; add the two verified PNGRB refs + the GAIL network-report ref to Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Length/Location/Owner
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/OWNER: confirmed, strongly. The wiki's own cite #1 (PNGRB's 14-Mar-2011 authorization-acceptance letter, No.Infra/PL/Exis/17/MUM-REG/GAIL/01/11, https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/ngp/Govt-Authorization/letter26april03.pdf) is a scanned image PDF (url_verifier returns 200/OK but can't text-match an image - false negative, not a broken link). I downloaded it and OCR'd it (tesseract, 300dpi): it is PNGRB's formal acceptance of GAIL's authorization to operate the 'Mumbai regional natural gas pipeline network as common carrier pipeline network,' addressed to GAIL's CMD, with an Annex-I table titled 'GAIL'S MUMBAI REGIONAL GAS PIPELINE NETWORK' breaking the system into two sub-networks: (A) Uran-Thal-Usar (Uran-RCF-Thal, Thal-Usar, Usar-Thal-IIL, IIL-H.R.Johnson, Usar-Khanav SVs), and (B) Trombay (Trombay-RCF, Trombay-MGL, Trombay-TPC) -- exactly matching GEM's StartLocation=Uran/EndLocation=Trombay. This independently confirms existence, GAIL as sole owner/operator, PipelineType=transmission (it is authorized as a common-carrier transmission pipeline under PNGRB regulation, not a city-gas/CGD distribution network), and Fuel=Gas. Not a duplicate of anything else in the India-gas roster: P0944 (Mumbai-Uran Trunk Line, 204 km) and P0926 (Heera-Uran Trunk Line, 80 km) are ONGC offshore-to-onshore trunk lines feeding Uran from the Bombay High fields, physically distinct from this GAIL common-carrier distribution network that moves gas onward from Uran/RCF/Thal/Usar to Trombay-area consumers (RCF, MGL, TPC, DFPCL). Cross-checked against the current PNGRB monthly NGPL-MIS report (data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, and the finer-precision 20250630 edition) -- both large text PDFs url_verifier flags as 200/OK-but-content-not-found (documented large-PDF false negative in this SOP); I fetched each and ran pdftotext -layout locally and confirmed the row by eye. Both list 'Mumbai Regional Network / GAIL / 14.03.2011' under the OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER section (not partially-commissioned or under-construction), i.e. Status=operating is current and correct as of at least June 2025 and May 2026. SPEC -- LengthKnown 128.68 km: the 2011 letter's Annex-I table totals exactly 128.68 km (19.50+20.00+20.00+27.53+20.00+6.00+1.20+4.20+5.50+7.70+0.05); the 20250630 PNGRB MIS report independently lists Authorised Length = 129.0 km (rounds to the same figure) as of 2025. Confirmed, exact. SPEC -- Capacity 7.04 MMSCMD: the 2011 letter gives declared system capacity of 3.542 MMSCMD (Uran-Thal-Usar) + 3.494 MMSCMD (Trombay) = 7.036, rounding to 7.04; the 20250630 PNGRB MIS report independently lists Authorised Capacity = 7.04 MMSCMD for 2025 -- exact match, two dates fifteen years apart, both from the regulator. As a THIRD, non-PNGRB-authored source I also found and skimmed GAIL's own 'Report for Capacity Assessment [of the] Integrated/Interconnected Pipeline Network' (a GAIL-authored technical filing hosted as a PNGRB public notice, https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/public-notice/GAIL_Report_Annx_19042024.pdf, also a large PDF url_verifier can't text-match -- confirmed locally), which names 'Uran-Thal-Usar sub-network of the Mumbai Regional Pipeline Network (UTU)' and 'Trombay-RFC sub-network of the Mumbai Regional Pipeline Network' as components of GAIL's integrated system feeding/fed by ONGCL Uran, RCF Trombay, MGL, DFPCL Taloja -- independent (company-authored, not the regulator's own compilation) corroboration of the network's existence, owner and endpoints. CAVEAT (not material, not flagged as a concern): the current PNGRB MIS report's 'Operating Length' field reads 125 (125.44 per a June-2025 web-search snippet), about 3.2 km short of the 128.68/129.0 authorised total -- normal for these filings (a small idle/spur segment, e.g. the 1.2 km Usar-Khanav SV branch, can sit outside the actively-flowing common-carrier length while the network as a whole stays classified operational); GEM's LengthKnown tracking the authorised/built total rather than the month's flowing-length figure is a reasonable and defensible choice, not an error. Diameter is correctly left blank: the network has ~7 different pipe diameters across its sub-sections (26in down to 4in per Annex-I) with no single figure to report. StartYear1 is correctly left blank: the 2011 letter states GAIL's own completion dates for the underlying pipe 'are from year 1978 to year 1998' -- a 20-year range across many segments, not a single commissioning year; per this run's guidance, the 2011 authorization date must never be used as a StartYear proxy, and a blank field is preferable to picking an arbitrary year from that range. Net verdict: real, correctly classified, correctly owned, and both Length and Capacity independently corroborated to 2 decimal places by two dated instances of the same regulator's data plus one GAIL-authored filing -- tier=high.

summary: P0943 confirmed real, correctly classified/owned (GAIL, transmission common carrier), not a duplicate of P0944/P0926; Length 128.68 km and Capacity 7.04 MMSCMD both exactly corroborated against PNGRB's 2011 authorization letter Annex-I and the current PNGRB NGPL-MIS report, plus a GAIL-authored network filing as a third source -- verdict confirmed (caveat: authorised vs. current flowing 'operating' length differ by ~3 km, not material).
